texts.li: [tribal] {X_nameDef}, a gray-haired hunter of {FACTION}, came into the camp with a pack that clanks when it's set down. {X_nameDef} has walked every trail between here and the sea, and is done walking.\n\nThe gear goes to whoever can use it: a fine weapon and good hides, worn but sound, for {COUNT} silver. Or the colony could ask {X_objective} to stay.

[medieval] {X_nameDef}, an old sellsword of {FACTION}, has stopped at the colony on the way home. Forty years of fighting other people's battles, {X_nameDef} says, and now all {X_pronoun} wants is a garden and a chair in the sun.\n\nThe gear is for sale: a well-kept blade and a coat of armor that has turned a great deal of steel. {X_nameDef} asks {COUNT} silver for the lot. Or the colony could ask {X_objective} to stay.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} spent thirty years as a hired gun and has the scars to prove it. Now {X_nameDef} is retiring, and selling the kit: a well-kept weapon and armor that has stopped more than one bullet. The price is {COUNT} silver.\n\nOr the colony could ask {X_objective} to stay.

An old adventurer, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, has stopped at the colony with a pack full of gear and more stories than teeth. {X_nameDef} is done with the road and wants to sell the lot, a fine weapon and armor kept in good order, for {COUNT} silver.\n\nOr the colony could ask {X_objective} to stay.

li.label: Buy the gear ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counts the silver and hands the gear over piece by piece, explaining where each dent came from.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay (may say no)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} looks around the colony for a long moment, then sets the pack down. The gear stays with {X_objective}, and so does {X_nameDef}.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} thinks it over through supper, then thanks the colony and says no: there's a sister down south {X_pronoun} hasn't seen in twenty years. {X_nameDef} tells stories until late before turning in.

li.label: An evening of stories
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sits up with the colony until late, telling of old fights, bad roads and the one time {X_pronoun} nearly got rich. In the morning {X_nameDef} sets off again, gear and all.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shoulders the pack again and heads on down the road.

texts.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a mapmaker of {FACTION}, is walking the hills with a measuring chain and a satchel of charts. {X_nameDef} offers to survey the colony's own land, and says a careful survey always turns up something in the rock.\n\nThe price is {COUNT} silver. Or, if {A_nameDef} guides {X_objective} around for a couple of days, {X_nameDef} will share whatever {X_pronoun} finds for nothing, though {X_pronoun} won't promise there'll be anything.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is mapping the region for {X_possessive} people, with a theodolite strapped to {X_possessive} pack and a tablet full of contour lines. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will survey the colony's land properly, and expects to find ore in the rock.\n\nWith {A_nameDef} as a guide, {X_nameDef} would do it for free, but quicker and rougher, with no promises.

{X_nameDef}, a mapmaker of {FACTION}, has asked to survey the hills around the colony. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will go over every slope and cliff face, and says there's always ore somewhere. If {A_nameDef} goes along as a guide, the survey costs nothing, but {X_nameDef} won't promise anything.

li.label: Pay for a survey ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} spends two days on the hills with chain and compass, and leaves a hand-drawn map of the colony's land with one place circled.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} guide {X_objective} (may find nothing)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walks the hills with {X_nameDef} for two days and learns more about mapmaking than {A_pronoun} expected. The survey is rough, but it cost nothing.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} walk the hills for two days and find nothing in the rock worth digging for. {A_nameDef} came back knowing a good deal about maps, at least.

li.label: Not today
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} folds up the charts and moves on to the next valley.

done.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef}'s survey found a seam of {THING} in the rock {PLACE}, close enough to the surface to dig out. It's marked with a cairn and a strip of red cloth.
[!lowtech] The survey turned up a seam of {THING} in the rock {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} marked it on the colony's map and sprayed an orange cross on the rock face before leaving.
{X_nameDef} found a seam of {THING} in the rock {PLACE}, and showed {A_nameDef} exactly where to start digging.

titles.li: [medieval] A monk of a silent order

texts.li: [tribal] A spirit-walker of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come to the camp with ash on {X_possessive} face. {X_nameDef} is keeping a season of silence, and asks with {X_possessive} hands for a place to sit near people for a day or two.\n\n{A_nameDef} has had a hard time of late, and has been watching the spirit-walker since {X_pronoun} came.

[medieval] {X_nameDef}, a monk of a silent order from {FACTION}'s lands, came to the gate with a slate and a stub of chalk. On the slate: a place to sit, a day or two, near people. Then I will go.\n\n{A_nameDef}, who hasn't been sleeping well, keeps finding reasons to walk past the gate.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has kept a vow of silence for four years, according to a worn card {X_pronoun} hands over at the gate. The card also asks for a place to sit near the colony for a day or two, and promises no trouble.\n\n{A_nameDef} read the card twice and hasn't gone far from the gate since.

[troubled] A silent traveler of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has asked by gestures for a place to sit near the colony for a day or two. {X_nameDef} doesn't speak and doesn't seem to need to.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been having a bad time lately, and hasn't taken {A_possessive} eyes off the stranger.

li.label: Let {X_objective} stay
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sits by the fields from dawn until dark, hands folded. People find themselves going over to sit nearby for a while, and coming back calmer.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to sit with {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} sit side by side for most of a day without a word between them. That night {A_nameDef} sleeps straight through until morning.

li.label: Send {X_objective} on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} bows and walks on down the road.

done.li: [sat] {TALE}, the silent guest, was gone before anyone was up. On the bench where {A_nameDef} and the guest sat together, there's a gift left behind: {ITEM}.
[stayed] {TALE}, the silent guest, left before dawn without a sound. On the bench by the fields there's something for the colony: {ITEM}.
By morning {TALE} had gone on, leaving a gift set neatly on the bench: {ITEM}.

texts.li: [leg] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} makes artificial limbs, and travels with a cart of them in every size. {X_nameDef} saw {A_nameDef} crossing the yard and stopped to offer {A_objective} a {TALE}, made to measure and fitted before {X_pronoun} leaves.\n\nThe price is {COUNT} silver, or {PLACE} in materials.

[foot] {X_nameDef}, a limb-maker of {FACTION}, watched {A_nameDef} limp across the yard and has offered to fit {A_objective} with a {TALE}. {X_nameDef} already has the measurements in {X_possessive} head.\n\nThe price is {COUNT} silver, or {PLACE} in materials.

[arm] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} builds and fits artificial limbs, and has offered to fit {A_nameDef} with a {TALE} before moving on. {X_nameDef} has fitted hundreds, {X_pronoun} says, and none of them has come back.\n\nThe price is {COUNT} silver, or {PLACE} in materials.

[jaw] {X_nameDef}, a maker of false parts from {FACTION}, has offered {A_nameDef} a {TALE}, carved and fitted while {X_pronoun} waits. {A_nameDef} hasn't eaten anything chewier than porridge in a long time.\n\nThe price is {COUNT} silver, or {PLACE} in materials.
A limb-maker of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, is passing through, and has offered to fit {A_nameDef} with a {TALE}. The price is {COUNT} silver, or {PLACE} in materials.

li.label: Pay {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} measures, carves and fits for most of the day, and by evening {A_nameDef} has a {TALE}.

li.label: Pay in materials ({PLACE})
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} measures, carves and fits for most of the day, and by evening {A_nameDef} has a {TALE}.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} packs up the cart and moves on.

li.label: Pay a little to have {X_objective} teach our best crafter
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} spent the day showing {B_nameDef} how a {TALE} is measured, shaped and fitted. {A_nameDef} goes without for now, and {B_nameDef} has a notebook full of measurements.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef} sat {B_nameDef} down with a block of ash and showed {B_objective} how a {TALE} is carved, joint by joint. {A_nameDef} goes without for now, and the offcuts are all over the workshop floor.
[leg] {X_nameDef} spends the day measuring, fitting and padding. By evening {A_nameDef} is walking the length of the colony on the new {TALE}, slowly at first, then again, faster.
[foot] {X_nameDef} has the {TALE} fitted by midday. {A_nameDef} spends the afternoon walking back and forth across the yard, trying it on every kind of ground.
[arm] {X_nameDef} works on the fitting until dark. By the end of it {A_nameDef} can pick up a cup with the new {TALE}, and has picked up every cup in the kitchen to be sure.
[jaw] {X_nameDef} carves and fits the {TALE} in an afternoon. At supper {A_nameDef} eats the toughest piece of meat in the pot, slowly and with great satisfaction.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a merchant of {FACTION}, is raising silver for a caravan to the coast and back, and has asked the colony to put some in. {X_nameDef} promises twice the stake back in about ten days, and talks very fast about the price of salt.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been listening carefully. Caravans get lost, and merchants aren't always merchants.

[trader] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} knew {A_nameDef} back in the trading days, and greeted {A_objective} like a long-lost cousin. {X_nameDef} is putting together a caravan venture and wants the colony in on it: twice the stake back in about ten days.\n\n{A_nameDef} says {X_nameDef} was honest, back then. Mostly.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is fitting out a trade run across the wastes and looking for backers. Put silver in now, {X_nameDef} says, and get twice as much back in about ten days, when the trucks return.\n\nIt could be a good deal. It could also be the last the colony sees of its silver, and {A_nameDef} is watching {X_nameDef} closely.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a merchant of {FACTION}, is buying a string of pack mules for a run to the salt towns and needs backers. {X_nameDef} offers twice the stake back in about ten days, sealed with a handshake and a scratched receipt.\n\n{A_nameDef} thinks the mules are real. {A_nameDef} isn't sure about the rest.

li.label: Put in {COUNT} silver (it may not come back)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counts the silver twice, writes out a receipt and shakes {A_nameDef}'s hand. The caravan should be back in about ten days.

li.label: Put in {TALE} silver (it may not come back)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} would have liked more, but takes the silver, writes out a receipt and shakes {A_nameDef}'s hand. The caravan should be back in about ten days.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} takes the refusal with good grace and goes off to find other backers.

extra.li: The colony has {ITEM} silver in its stores.

coming.li: {TALE}'s caravan venture, with {COUNT} of the colony's silver in it, is due back in about {DAYS}.

done.li: [good] {TALE}'s caravan came back from the venture with empty packs and full purses, and {TALE} has paid out the colony's share: {COUNT} silver, counted out at the gate.
[good,lowtech] A rider from {FACTION} brought the colony's share of {TALE}'s venture today: {COUNT} silver in a knotted sack, and a note saying the salt sold well.

[lost] Bad news from {FACTION}: {TALE}'s caravan was caught by a storm in the passes and lost most of its goods. {TALE} sent what could be saved of the colony's stake, {COUNT} silver, with an apology.
[lost] {TALE}'s caravan never reached the coast. Bandits took most of it in the second week. {TALE} came back alone and handed over {COUNT} silver, all that was left of the colony's share.

fail.li: {TALE}'s caravan should have been back days ago. Word from {FACTION}'s lands is that no merchant by that name is known there, and no caravan ever left for the coast. The colony's silver is gone.
The receipt {TALE} wrote out has turned out to be worth exactly the paper it's on. There was never any caravan, and there won't be any silver.

texts.li: Riders of {FACTION} came to the gate with a question. They've heard the colony holds {X_nameDef} of {ENEMY}, who raided one of their villages last year, and they want {X_objective}. They'll pay {COUNT} silver to take {X_objective} back to stand trial.\n\nThey don't say what kind of trial.

[lowtech] A party of {FACTION} rode up under their banner and asked for the colony's prisoner by name. {X_nameDef} of {ENEMY} burned one of their farms and killed a herdsman, they say, and they'll pay {COUNT} silver to have {X_objective} handed over.\n\nThey don't say what will happen to {X_nameDef} after that.

[!lowtech] {FACTION} have sent a message: the colony is holding {X_nameDef}, a raider of {ENEMY} they've been after for a year. They're offering {COUNT} silver to collect {X_objective}, and they can have people at the gate today.\n\nThe message doesn't say what they mean to do with {X_objective}.

li.label: Hand {X_objective} over ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {FACTION}'s people put {X_nameDef} in irons and take {X_objective} away. The silver is left at the gate.

li.label: Release {X_objective} instead
li.outcome: The wardens are told to let {X_nameDef} go. {FACTION}'s people leave without another word.

li.label: Keep {X_objective} here
li.outcome: The colony keeps its prisoner. {FACTION}'s people ride off, not pleased.

remembered.li: {ENEMY} haven't forgotten that the colony sold {TALE} to {FACTION}.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} found someone in the brush beyond the fields: {X_nameDef}, half-conscious, with a bad wound and a weapon {X_pronoun} wouldn't let go of. {X_nameDef} won't say who did it or why, only that {X_pronoun} needs somewhere to lie low.\n\nWhoever did it might come looking.

[winter] Out on the land, {A_nameDef} found tracks in the snow, then blood, then {X_nameDef}, curled up under a ledge and shaking. {X_nameDef} is hurt and armed, and won't say how {X_pronoun} got hurt.\n\nLeft out there tonight, {X_nameDef} may not see morning. Whoever did this may still be out there too.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} came back from the woods with news: a stranger, {X_nameDef}, is lying hurt in a hollow by the stream, with a blade in {X_possessive} hand that {X_pronoun} won't put down. {X_nameDef} asks for help and won't answer any questions.\n\nSomeone did that to {X_objective}, and they may not be finished.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} found {X_nameDef} slumped against a rock beyond the fields, with a field dressing soaked through and a rifle across {X_possessive} knees. {X_nameDef} won't say who did it, only that {X_pronoun} needs a place to lie low.\n\nWhoever did it may still be looking.

li.label: Bring {X_objective} in (someone may come looking)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is carried in and put to bed. As soon as {X_pronoun} can stand, {X_nameDef} says, {X_pronoun} will earn {X_possessive} place.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} is carried in and put to bed. Before dawn the watch spots riders on the far ridge, asking after {X_nameDef}: {ENEMY}. They'll be back for {X_objective} within a few days.

li.label: {ENEMY} want {X_nameDef}
li.text: {ENEMY} have tracked {X_nameDef} to the colony, and they've come to finish what they started.

li.label: Leave food and bandages (may be repaid)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} leaves food, water and clean bandages beside {X_nameDef} and walks away. By the next morning {X_nameDef} is gone.

li.label: Leave {X_objective} there
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walks away, and doesn't go back to look.

done.li: [lowtech] Someone left a bundle at the gate in the night, wrapped in oilcloth and tied with a strip of old bandage. Inside: {ITEM}, and a strip of bark with a name cut into it, {TALE}.
[!lowtech] A bundle was left at the gate overnight, tied up with a length of old bandage. Inside: {ITEM}, and a scrap of paper with a name on it, {TALE}.
The night watch heard footsteps at the gate and found a bundle there in the morning: {ITEM}. It's tied with a bandage of the kind the colony left for {TALE}.

titles.li: [medieval] A herald under a white flag

texts.li: [tribal] A pipe-bearer of {ENEMY} has come alone and sat down in the grass beyond the fields with a carved pipe across {X_possessive} knees. {X_nameDef} has come to talk of ending the feud.\n\nThe price of peace is {COUNT} silver, or {TALE}. The pipe stays unlit until it's paid.

[medieval] A herald of {ENEMY} waits on the road below the colony under a white flag. {X_nameDef} carries an offer: {ENEMY} will put up their swords if the colony pays {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} from its stores, as the price of the blood between them.

[!lowtech] {ENEMY} have sent an envoy, {X_nameDef}, who waits outside the colony under a white flag with empty hands held where the colony's guards can see them. The offer is short: {COUNT} silver, or {TALE}, and the fighting stops.
{X_nameDef}, an envoy of {ENEMY}, has come up the road to the colony unarmed. {ENEMY} are tired of the feud, {X_nameDef} says, and will make peace for {COUNT} silver, or {TALE}.

li.label: Pay {COUNT} silver for peace
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} takes the silver back to {ENEMY}. By nightfall word comes back: the feud is over, for now.

li.label: Pay {TALE} for peace
li.outcome: The food is carried out to the envoy, and {ENEMY} send carts for it before dark. The feud is over, for now.

li.label: Send the envoy away
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back to {ENEMY} with nothing to show for the walk. The feud goes on.

remembered.li: {FACTION} have kept the peace since their envoy came.
The peace with {FACTION} was bought, and so far it's holding.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, reeve to a lord of {FACTION}, rode in this morning with a ledger under {X_possessive} arm. By {X_nameDef}'s reckoning the colony's fields lie inside the lord's lands, and the lord's lands owe a tithe: {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} in kind, to be carried to {PLACE}.\n\n{A_nameDef} doubts the colony's land was ever in anyone's ledger, and would like to say so.

[fall] The harvest is in, and with it comes {X_nameDef}, reeve to a lord of {FACTION}, to collect the tithe. The colony owes {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} says, or {TALE} from its stores, for land the lord's grandfather once rode across.\n\n{A_nameDef} would very much like to see the deed.

A reeve of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come with two men-at-arms and a wax seal to collect a tithe for the lord at {PLACE}: {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} in kind. The colony has never paid anyone a tithe before.\n\n{A_nameDef} thinks it shouldn't start now, and is ready to argue the point.

li.label: Pay {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} weighs the silver, writes the colony into the ledger and rides off.

li.label: Pay in kind ({TALE})
li.outcome: {X_nameDef}'s men load the sacks onto a wagon, and the colony is written into the ledger.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} dispute it (losing costs more)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} argues the boundaries stone by stone until {X_nameDef} gives up and shuts the ledger. The lord, {X_nameDef} says, will look into it.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} argues, but {X_nameDef} has the deed, the seal and all afternoon. The colony pays the tithe, and a fine on top for wasting the reeve's time.

li.label: Refuse
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} writes something long in the ledger and rides off. {FACTION} won't think well of the colony for a while.

texts.li: [!lowtech] A survey drone came down {PLACE} this morning, trailing smoke, and split its casing on the rocks. It carries {FACTION}'s markings.\n\n{A_nameDef} thinks there's still something in its memory: maps, scans, maybe more. It could also be stripped for parts, or sent back to {FACTION}, who would likely pay to have it back.

[spacer] A {FACTION} scout drone dropped out of the sky {PLACE} with a dead thruster and buried its nose in the dirt. Its core is still blinking.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to try pulling data off it before the core wipes itself. It could also be stripped for parts, or returned to its owners for a reward.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} heard a whine and a crunch {PLACE}, and found a drone of {FACTION}'s nose-down in a furrow of torn earth, one rotor still turning.\n\nIts memory might hold something worth having, if {A_nameDef} can get into it before it wipes. Otherwise it's good for parts, or {FACTION} would pay for its return.

li.label: Strip it for parts
li.outcome: The drone is taken apart down to the last bolt: components, steel, and a tangle of wire that goes on the scrap pile.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} pull its memory (it may wipe itself)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} gets into the drone's memory before it can wipe, and spends the evening copying survey data and sensor logs. Some of it bears on the colony's own research.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} gets the casing open, but the core wipes itself the moment {A_pronoun} touches it. One component is all that's left worth having.

li.label: Return it to {FACTION} ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {FACTION} send someone to collect the wreck, with {COUNT} silver and their thanks.

texts.li: [!lowtech] The comms console has picked up the same short signal every hour since dawn: a call sign, a string of numbers, then silence. {A_nameDef} thinks it's coming from somewhere close.\n\nAnswering it would tell whoever is listening where the colony is. {A_nameDef} could also try to trace it without answering.

[spacer] A weak signal keeps coming through on the comms, a looped call for help in an old spacer code. It could be a survivor, a beacon that never stopped calling, or bait.\n\n{A_nameDef} can try to trace it without answering, or the colony can answer it.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} has been sitting at the comms all morning listening to a faint voice repeat the same three words on an old frequency, over and over. The recording has a date on it that's years old.\n\nThe colony could answer. {A_nameDef} could also try to find where it's coming from without giving the colony away.

li.label: Answer it (it may be a lure)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} answers the signal.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} answers, and the signal cuts off mid-word. An hour later another channel lights up with laughter and the colony's own coordinates read back. {ENEMY} are coming.

li.label: {ENEMY} answer back
li.text: The signal was bait. {ENEMY} traced the colony's answer, and have come to see what they caught.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} trace it without answering
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} narrows the signal down over a long afternoon, to a spot out on the colony's own land.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} chases the signal across three bands until it fades out for good. Whatever it was, it's gone.

li.label: Leave it
li.outcome: The signal is left to repeat itself. By evening it has stopped.

outcomes.li: [survivor] {A_nameDef} answers, and a hoarse voice comes back: {X_nameDef}, alone in a damaged escape pod for days. {A_nameDef} talks {X_objective} down toward the colony, and the pod is coming in now.

[survivor] {A_nameDef} answers, and after a long silence a voice says thank you, three times. It's {X_nameDef}, the last one left on a drifting wreck, with one pod still working. The pod is on its way down.
[beacon] {A_nameDef} answers. Nothing answers back. It's an automated beacon, still calling from a wreck that was picked clean years ago.
[beacon] {A_nameDef} answers, and gets an automated reply: the same call sign, the same numbers. Whoever set the beacon running is long gone.

done.li: The signal came from an old transmitter buried {PLACE}, wired to a supply cache that nobody ever came back for. {A_nameDef} dug it out: {ITEM}.
{A_nameDef} followed the signal to a rusted beacon half sunk in the ground {PLACE}. Beside it, under a tarp gone stiff with age, was what someone meant to come back for: {ITEM}.

texts.li: [gifted] {X_nameDef}, a wandering scholar of {FACTION}, has a book wrapped in oilcloth at the bottom of {X_possessive} pack: {THING}. It's the real thing, {X_nameDef} swears, and it opens only to someone with the gift.\n\n{A_nameDef} has the gift, and hasn't been able to look away from it since it came out of the pack. {X_nameDef} asks {COUNT} silver.

[ungifted] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} sells old books off the back of a mule, and one of them is the real thing: {THING}. The colony has no one with the gift to use it yet, {X_nameDef} admits, but books like this are rare, and the right person may come along.\n\nThe price is {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Buy it ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} unwraps the book, lets {A_nameDef} hold it for a moment and takes the silver.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} wraps the book up again and moves on.
